title: Hash tables (the dictionary that never searches)
description:
Compy finds a name in a million without looking through a million. Hash tables turn a key into a location.

#hashtable #python #datastructures #shorts
angle: A hash table finds a value by computing where it lives from the key, instead of searching for it.
hook: How does Python find one key in a dictionary of a million, without checking them all?

scenes.speaker: byte
scenes.narration: How does Python find one key in a dictionary of a million, without checking them all?

scenes.speaker: compy
scenes.narration: Short version: it doesn't search. It calculates. Three parts: the hash, the bucket, the collision.

props.heading: In this episode
items: Turning a key into a number

scenes.speaker: byte
scenes.narration: So a hash function eats a key and spits out a number?

scenes.speaker: compy
scenes.narration: Same key, same number, every time within one run. That number picks the bucket. No scanning.

scenes.speaker: byte
scenes.narration: Like a coat check. The ticket number is the hook.

scenes.speaker: compy
scenes.narration: Fine. A tidier coat check than most. But eventually two keys land on the same hook.

scenes.speaker: byte
scenes.narration: That's a collision. So the whole thing breaks?

scenes.speaker: compy
scenes.narration: No. The table compares keys, and keeps both. Collisions are normal, just rare when the table has room.

props.code:
# lookup, roughly
b = hash(key) % size
if keys match: return value
else: probe the next slot

scenes.speaker: byte
scenes.narration: So lookups are constant time. Basically instant.

scenes.speaker: compy
scenes.narration: That's why a dict beats a list when you ask whether an item exists. Try it.

scenes.speaker: byte
scenes.narration: Rule of the day: need to look things up fast? Use a dict.

props.label: TODAY'S RULE
props.rule: Lookup by key? Use a dict

scenes.speaker: compy
scenes.narration: Follow for more. Next: why caching is easy until the data changes.

claims.text: A hash table maps keys to values by using a hash function to compute an index into an array of buckets
Python dict lookup is O(1) on average and O(n) in the worst case
Python's built-in hash() of strings is randomized per process, so values differ between runs
